text:
mara: seeing a weird spike in connection resets from the edge proxies in us-west-2, lots of short-lived client fds then pods OOM/restart :confused:
ben: timeline? did something deploy around then?
mara: no deployments; started ~09:04, peaked 09:07, ~1k conn resets/min for a few mins, then fell back at 09:12
amy: can you paste the logs/snippets? curious if it's SYN backlog or ephemeral port reuse
mara: paste: ```
09:06:45 proxy-1 kernel: [net] TCP: RST from remote, errno=104
09:06:45 proxy-1 app: upstream connect failed: ECONNRESET
09:06:46 proxy-1 ss -s: TCP: * total: 8923 (established 120, closed 8600)
conntrack entries: 12345
` ```
ben: that closed>established ratio screams ephemeral port exhaustion; check ephemeral range & TIME_WAIT counts
nathan: ran quick check from a hit node: ```
$ sysctl net.ipv4.ip_local_port_range
net.ipv4.ip_local_port_range = 32768    60999
$ ss -tan state TIME-WAIT | wc -l
48000
$ cat /proc/net/nf_conntrack | wc -l
148000
```
zoe: yeah 48k TIME_WAIT on that node, local ports only ~28k usable -> immediate churn
mamara: (typo) mara: interesting — connection reuse policy + many short connections to S3/model-puller could be causing hitting port ceiling
ben: two quick mitigation ideas: 1) move model pulls to fewer long-lived workers w/ connection pooling, 2) add NAT capacity (another NAT GW or scale via EIPs)
amy: also: reduce ephemeral port TIME_WAIT by tuning tcp_tw_reuse/tcp_tw_recycle? careful with reuse across NAT but tcp_tw_reuse=1 helps. prefer keepalives and connection pooling though
ops-bot: deploy triggered: edge-proxy 2.14.1 restart at 09:18 (automated circuit breaker)
zoe: ops-bot noted restarts — that created a thundering reconnection wave, probably amplified exhaustion
mara: action plan proposed: short-term add 2x NAT GW attachments to affected AZ + flip edge-proxy to connection pool mode (flagged)
ben: can we test ephemeral port headroom with a small loadtest? I can run a 10k ephemeral client sim to confirm mitigation impact
nathan: I'll open a ticket to patch model puller to maintain 1 persistent connection per worker instead of per model request (low-risk change)
amy: I'll prepare a NAT capacity playbook: steps to attach additional NATs, route table changes, rollback instructions, expected DNS/conn impacts
zoe: also consider node-local egress proxy (squid/nginx sidecar) to multiplex connections and conserve source ports long-term
mara: temporary config tweak we applied: net.ipv4.tcp_tw_reuse=1 on the hotspots; monitoring looks better at 09:30 (TIME_WAIT down ~60%)
ben: +1 on pragmatic short-term. but long-term we need connection pooling and either eni/extra nat or node-local egress as zoe said
zoe: leaving link to notes/playbook: https://internal.redwood/intra/playbooks/nat-capacity-add-az (draft) :eyes:
amy: logging follow-up: add conntrack and TIME_WAIT dashboards for per-az breakouts and alert when available ephemeral ports < 20%
mara: thx all — keeping an eye, will update if it reoccurs. tagging @oncall for follow-up
ben: great. one more: recommend we baseline per-model-pull fanout and add a guardrail in autoscaler to limit simultaneous pulls per node
mara: noted. closing thread when oncall ack recorded. :thumbsup:
